one_liner: C++ packet capture, parsing and crafting library; parses pcap TCP/DNS traffic 1.06-1.26x faster than libtins in its maintainers' run.
what_it_does: PcapPlusPlus is three libraries: Packet++ (parse, edit and craft 60 protocols, from Ethernet and IPv4 to DNS, TLS, QUIC and BGP), Pcap++ (C++ wrappers over libpcap, Npcap, DPDK, AF_XDP, PF_RING, WinDivert and raw sockets, plus pcap/pcapng file readers and writers) and Common++. You read a RawPacket from a device or file, wrap it in pcpp::Packet, and walk a linked list of typed Layer objects (getLayerOfType<TcpLayer>() and so on). It is not a drop-in for libtins: libtins hands you an owning PDU tree, PcapPlusPlus hands you layer views over one raw buffer, and the two APIs share nothing.
how_it_is_fast: Each Layer is a typed view into the RawPacket's single buffer, so headers and payloads are read in place and no per-layer copy is made; libtins by contrast copies the payload into a RawPDU std::vector (742 bytes per packet in this benchmark) and decodes every TCP option into a vector when it builds the TCP PDU. PcapPlusPlus still allocates one object per layer at Packet construction (all layers are parsed eagerly unless you pass parseUntil), but TCP options are only walked on demand through a TLV reader (getTcpOption), and DNS answer data is decoded only when asked. Much of the measured margin is therefore copy avoidance and deferred option decoding, not a faster parser for the same work.
when_to_use: Offline analysis of pcap/pcapng files where most packets are only classified or counted by layer type, so zero-copy layer views and on-demand option decoding pay off.
Applications that need one C++ API across capture engines: libpcap on Linux/macOS/FreeBSD, Npcap on Windows, and DPDK, AF_XDP or PF_RING for line-rate capture.
Tools that need protocol coverage libtins lacks (QUIC, TLS records, SSH, BGP, GTP, SOME/IP, Modbus, LDAP, X509) or built-in TCP reassembly, IP defragmentation and JA3/JA3S fingerprinting.
Projects that want a permissive licence: the Unlicense places it in the public domain, so it can be vendored without attribution.
when_not_to_use: When you need every TCP option or DNS record decoded for every packet anyway: the libtins gap then shrinks toward the 1.06x TCP-without-options result, and libtins's owning PDU objects may suit your code better.
When you only need to count or hash raw frames: plain libpcap was 1.6x (TCP) to 6.7x (DNS) faster in the same run because it skips parsing and the per-packet copy and allocations.
Concurrent edits: the maintainer states a Packet or Layer must be parsed and edited on one thread; there is no internal locking.

Builds pinned to unreleased master between the libpcap-free pcap reader change (commit 44e9085, after v25.05) and the fix in PR #2072 (March 2026): issue #2071 measured pcap file reading 22x slower than v25.05 (1.857 s vs 0.084 s for 485,760 packets).

integration.form: static lib by default (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF; shared optional): Common++, Packet++ and Pcap++; also packaged in vcpkg, Conan, Homebrew
integration.dependencies: Packet++/Common++: none beyond the standard library; Pcap++: libpcap (Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, Android) or Npcap/WinPcap (Windows), optional DPDK, PF_RING, libbpf/AF_XDP, WinDivert; can be built without Pcap++ (PCAPPP_BUILD_PCAPPP=OFF)
integration.min_toolchain: C++14 and CMake 3.12 on current master (v24.09, the benchmarked release, required C++11); the project's CMake defaults to a Release build
integration.platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS, Android, FreeBSD; x86-64 and aarch64; DPDK, PF_RING and AF_XDP back-ends are Linux-only
integration.thread_safety: Not thread-safe per object: per the maintainer (issue #703), a Packet or Layer is parsed/edited on one thread and may then be read from others; devices and reassembly objects are the application's job to synchronise.

gotchas: Harness asymmetry in the 'TCP with options' test (the 1.19x row): the callback only counts packets, so PcapPlusPlus never decodes the options (TcpLayer's constructor does nothing with them), while libtins's TCP constructor decodes all six generated options into a vector. PcapPlusPlus's time grows 5 ms over the no-options test, libtins's 32 ms; the row measures eager versus deferred option decoding, not equal work.

pcpp::Packet(&rawPacket) parses every layer eagerly and allocates one object per layer (and one per DNS resource, with its name decoded into a std::string); pass parseUntil/parseUntilLayer to stop early when you only need the lower layers.
Layer pointers and DnsQuery/DnsResource pointers are owned by the Packet and dangle once it (or the RawPacket buffer) is destroyed or edited in a way that reallocates the buffer.
Parser hardening is still ongoing: recent master commits fix out-of-bounds reads in the WireGuard, ASN.1 and S7Comm layers found by OSS-Fuzz targets; no CVE or GitHub security advisory is published.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the catalogued event-loops-io siblings parses packets: F-Stack, mTCP and Seastar are DPDK-based TCP stacks or servers, and libuv/libevent-style loops (libev, libhv, picoev) move bytes over sockets. Pick PcapPlusPlus when the task is decoding or crafting captured frames, possibly on top of DPDK or AF_XDP, rather than serving connections.
verified_claims_summary: The PcapPlusPlus website's benchmark page (maintainers' run) used mfontanini/packet-capture-benchmarks with PcapPlusPlus v24.09, libtins v4.5 and libpcap 1.10.1, g++ 11.4.0, on Ubuntu 22.04 under WSL2 on an i7-8700: over a generated 500,000-packet pcap (742-byte payload, integer-millisecond average of 3 runs) PcapPlusPlus took 0.197/0.202/0.208 s for TCP, TCP-with-options and DNS against libtins's 0.209/0.241/0.263 s (1.06x, 1.19x, 1.26x, derived from page data), and was slower than a libpcap loop that only counts packets. The TCP-with-options and DNS rows do unequal work (deferred options; libtins re-parses and materialises DNS vectors), and library build flags are not stated (project defaults would be -O3 Release for PcapPlusPlus and -O2 RelWithDebInfo for libtins).
status_note: Actively maintained (commits through 2026-10-09, 3.1k stars, 2,698 commits, frequent fuzz-driven fixes) and public domain under the Unlicense, which has no patent grant; the benchmark page is first-party and predates the master-branch pcap reader rewrite, so its numbers describe v24.09.
